front_blocks.md: What is a **molecular formula**?

back_blocks.md: A **molecular formula** shows the types of atoms in a molecule (given by chemical symbols) and the number of each type of atom (given by subscript numbers).

cards.front_md: What is a **molecular formula**?
cards.back_md: A **molecular formula** shows the types of atoms in a molecule (given by chemical symbols) and the number of each type of atom (given by subscript numbers).

front_blocks.md: Seven elements exist as **diatomic molecules**, meaning each molecule contains **..........**  atoms of the same element.

back_blocks.md: Seven elements exist as **diatomic molecules**, meaning each molecule contains **two** atoms of the same element.
The seven diatomic elements are H<sub>2</sub>, N<sub>2</sub>, O<sub>2</sub>, F<sub>2</sub>, Cl<sub>2</sub>, Br<sub>2</sub> and I<sub>2</sub>.

cards.front_md: Seven elements exist as **diatomic molecules**, meaning each molecule contains **..........**  atoms of the same element.
cards.back_md:

The seven diatomic elements are H<sub>2</sub>, N<sub>2</sub>, O<sub>2</sub>, F<sub>2</sub>, Cl<sub>2</sub>, Br<sub>2</sub> and I<sub>2</sub>.

front_blocks.md: How many atoms of each element are present in sulfuric acid, H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>?

back_blocks.md: H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> contains 2 hydrogen atoms, 1 sulfur atom and 4 oxygen atoms.
The **subscript** number after each symbol gives the count; where no subscript is shown, there is 1 atom.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
All seven diatomic elements are non-metals.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
The seven diatomic elements — hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, fluorine, chlorine, bromine and iodine — are all **non-metals**.

front_blocks.md: What is an **ionic compound**?

back_blocks.md: An **ionic compound** is a compound formed when a metal reacts with a non-metal, producing positive metal ions and negative non-metal ions held together by electrostatic attraction.

cards.front_md: What is an **ionic compound**?
cards.back_md: An **ionic compound** is a compound formed when a metal reacts with a non-metal, producing positive metal ions and negative non-metal ions held together by electrostatic attraction.

front_blocks.md: What is the **swap-and-drop method** and when is it used to find an ionic formula?
**(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: The **swap-and-drop method** is used when two ions have different charges. The size of each ion's charge becomes the subscript of the other ion, giving the ratio that produces an overall neutral compound.

cards.front_md:
What is the **swap-and-drop method** and when is it used to find an ionic formula?

**(Extended Tier Only)**
cards.back_md: The **swap-and-drop method** is used when two ions have different charges. The size of each ion's charge becomes the subscript of the other ion, giving the ratio that produces an overall neutral compound.

front_blocks.md: In an ionic compound, the overall charge is **..........**  because the positive charges on the cations are cancelled by the negative charges on the anions.

back_blocks.md: In an ionic compound, the overall charge is **zero** because the positive charges on the cations are cancelled by the negative charges on the anions.

cards.front_md: In an ionic compound, the overall charge is **..........**  because the positive charges on the cations are cancelled by the negative charges on the anions.
cards.back_md: In an ionic compound, the overall charge is **zero** because the positive charges on the cations are cancelled by the negative charges on the anions.

front_blocks.md: What is the formula of copper(II) chloride, given that copper(II) ions are Cu<sup>2+</sup> and chloride ions are Cl<sup>-</sup>?
**(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: The formula is CuCl<sub>2</sub>.
One Cu<sup>2+</sup> ion requires two Cl<sup>-</sup> ions to cancel the overall charge, giving the **ratio** 1:2.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The carbonate ion has the formula CO<sub>3</sub><sup>2-</sup>.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
The **carbonate** ion, CO<sub>3</sub><sup>2-</sup>, is a **polyatomic ion** carrying a 2– charge, made of one carbon atom bonded to three oxygen atoms.

front_blocks.md: Why must the swap-and-drop method give the simplest whole-number ratio when the two ions have the **same** charge?
**(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: After swapping and dropping, **always simplify to the lowest whole-number ratio**.
When both ions carry the same charge the method gives, for example, Ca<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> — which must be simplified to **CaO**. Without that step the formula is wrong.

front_blocks.md: What is a **word equation**?

back_blocks.md: A **word equation** shows the reactants and products of a chemical reaction written as full chemical names, with reactants on the left and products on the right of an arrow.

cards.front_md: What is a **word equation**?
cards.back_md: A **word equation** shows the reactants and products of a chemical reaction written as full chemical names, with reactants on the left and products on the right of an arrow.

front_blocks.md: In a word equation, the substances on the left of the arrow are called **..........**  and the substances on the right are called **.........**.

back_blocks.md: In a word equation, the substances on the left of the arrow are called **reactants** and the substances on the right are called **products**.

cards.front_md: In a word equation, the substances on the left of the arrow are called **..........**  and the substances on the right are called **.........**.
cards.back_md: In a word equation, the substances on the left of the arrow are called **reactants** and the substances on the right are called **products**.

front_blocks.md: Write the word equation for the reaction of ammonia with nitric acid.

back_blocks.md: **Ammonia** + **nitric acid** → **ammonium nitrate**.
Ammonia and nitric acid are the reactants; ammonium nitrate is the sole product.

cards.front_md: Write the word equation for the reaction of ammonia with nitric acid.
cards.back_md:
**Ammonia** + **nitric acid** → **ammonium nitrate**.

Ammonia and nitric acid are the reactants; ammonium nitrate is the sole product.

front_blocks.md: What is a **symbol equation**?

back_blocks.md: A **symbol equation** uses chemical formulas to represent reactants and products, showing the relative numbers of each species and must be balanced so atom counts are equal on both sides.

cards.front_md: What is a **symbol equation**?
cards.back_md: A **symbol equation** uses chemical formulas to represent reactants and products, showing the relative numbers of each species and must be balanced so atom counts are equal on both sides.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
When balancing an equation, you can change the subscript numbers in a formula.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
You can only change the **coefficients** (numbers in front of formulas). Changing subscripts would alter the identity of the substance.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

front_blocks.md: What are the four state symbols used in symbol equations and what does each represent?

back_blocks.md: The four state symbols are **(s)** for **solid**, **(l)** for **liquid**, **(g)** for **gas** and **(aq)** for **aqueous** (dissolved in water).

cards.front_md: What are the four state symbols used in symbol equations and what does each represent?
cards.back_md: The four state symbols are **(s)** for **solid**, **(l)** for **liquid**, **(g)** for **gas** and **(aq)** for **aqueous** (dissolved in water).

front_blocks.md: A symbol equation must be **balanced** so that the number of **..........**  of each element is the same on both sides of the arrow.

back_blocks.md: A symbol equation must be **balanced** so that the number of **atoms** of each element is the same on both sides of the arrow.
This reflects the law of conservation of mass.

front_blocks.md: Why is it useful to treat a polyatomic ion (e.g. NO<sub>3</sub><sup>–</sup>) as a single unit when balancing an equation?

back_blocks.md: Treating an unchanged **polyatomic ion** as a single unit simplifies the balancing process. If the group appears on both sides of the equation unchanged, counting it as one entity avoids errors from counting individual atoms separately.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Ionic equations must always include state symbols.
**(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: **True.**
**State symbols** are essential in ionic equations because they distinguish between species in solution (aq) and those that are solid, liquid or gaseous.

front_blocks.md: What are **spectator ions** and how are they identified in an ionic equation?
**(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: **Spectator ions** are ions that appear on both sides of a full ionic equation unchanged. They are removed from the ionic equation because they do not take part in the reaction.
